name: Alloy-Shallows
geological_features: Shallow seas averaging only 200 meters depth across most of the surface
Submerged coral plateaus visible from orbit
Perpetual storm systems in the equatorial band
specific_features: Pirate hideout established on a submerged atoll
description: Alloy-Shallows is a warm oceanic world remarkable for the uniformity of its seafloor: a vast, nearly flat expanse of mineral-rich sediment that rarely exceeds two hundred meters below the surface. The shallow waters create a world of extraordinary visibility, where the golden seabed is visible from the air and enormous shoals of metallic-scaled fish move in formations that glitter like flowing mercury. The dense atmosphere traps heat efficiently, keeping the waters bathwater-warm in the equatorial regions.

The air is heavy and humid, thick enough to feel like a substance rather than an absence. Storm systems build quickly over the warm shallows, generating towering cumulus formations that discharge spectacular lightning displays across the flat horizon. The shallow water absorbs and re-radiates heat, making nights nearly as warm as days and creating a perpetual sauna-like atmosphere that most visitors find either intoxicating or suffocating.

The shallowness of the ocean is itself a mystery, as no known geological process explains such uniform bathymetry across a planet-spanning body of water. Orbital scans have detected a dense metallic layer beneath the sediment that may be an alloy of natural or artificial origin, essentially a planetary-scale metal plate covered in a thin layer of ocean. A satellite graveyard in low orbit, remnants of various survey missions, attests to the difficulty of conducting orbital operations in the planet's magnetically turbulent environment.

A pirate syndicate has established operations on a submerged atoll, using the planet's magnetic interference to shield their activities from detection. Legitimate interest in the world centers on the metallic substrate, which if artificial would represent the largest known constructed object in the galaxy. The thriving marine ecosystem makes any invasive investigation politically sensitive, as environmental advocacy groups have designated the planet a protected biosphere.
